title: [Transport] ConnectionPoolOptions per-host connection limit defaults to 16 on desktop while the docs say 6
body:
## Summary
The per-host connection limit in ConnectionPoolOptions and the default pool in RawSocketTransport take PlatformConfig.RecommendedMaxConcurrency, which is 16 on Editor/desktop and 8 on mobile. The property and constructor doc comments say 6 on desktop and 8 on mobile. A desktop client fanning out to one origin therefore opens 16 parallel connections, which can trip per-client connection limits on servers and CDNs, and the documentation is wrong.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:56`

## Problem
ConnectionPoolOptions._maxConnectionsPerHost and the default pool in RawSocketTransport both take PlatformConfig.RecommendedMaxConcurrency (ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:56, RawSocketTransport.cs:70-72), which is documented as 'Recommended maximum concurrent requests' and is 16 for the Editor/desktop and 8 for iOS/Android (PlatformConfig.cs:22, :27, :53-57). The property doc says '(e.g., 6 on Desktop, 8 on Mobile)' (ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:69-70) and the pool constructor says 'default 6, matches browser convention' (TcpConnectionPool.cs:307, :321).

**Failure scenario.** A desktop client that fans out requests to one HTTP/1.1 origin opens 16 parallel connections (16 TLS handshakes, and 16 discarded dials per burst for an HTTP/2 origin, see net-runtime-05), enough to trip per-client connection limits on common servers and CDNs; the documentation tells the user the limit is 6.

## Suggested fix
Give the per-host limit its own constant (6, or 8 on mobile if that is intended) separate from the global request concurrency, and align the three doc comments with it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The per-host connection limit has its own constant, separate from RecommendedMaxConcurrency, with the intended value (6 on desktop, 8 on mobile if intended)
- [ ] The three doc comments in ConnectionPoolOptions and the pool constructor state the actual default
- [ ] A fan-out of 20 requests to one HTTP/1.1 origin opens no more than the documented limit of connections, covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after

title: [Architecture] HappyEyeballsOptions in TurboHTTP.Core is declared in namespace TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection
body:
## Summary
HappyEyeballsOptions is compiled into the Core assembly but declared in the TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection namespace, which contradicts the rule that namespaces are TurboHTTP.<Module>. Projects without the Transport assembly still see that namespace from Core, and user code configuring a Core option must import a Transport namespace. Moving the type later is a source-breaking change once the API is frozen.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:3`

## Problem
Runtime/Core/HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:3 declares 'namespace TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection' for a type built into the Core assembly; Runtime/Core/ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:2 needs 'using TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection;' to expose it as ConnectionPoolOptions.HappyEyeballs. architecture.md states 'Namespaces are TurboHTTP.<Module>' and that Core references no other assembly. The same namespace also holds the Transport assembly's own types (HappyEyeballsConnector, Nat64AddressSynthesizer, LocalhostNames).

**Failure scenario.** A project that omits TurboHTTP.Transport (custom transport, or WebGL where Transport is excluded) still sees a TurboHTTP.Transport.Connection namespace coming from Core, and user code that configures a Core client option must import a Transport namespace; a later move of the type to its documented namespace is a source-breaking change once the API is frozen.

## Suggested fix
Move HappyEyeballsOptions to namespace TurboHTTP.Core before the 1.0 API freeze (keeping the file where it is), and add the namespace-equals-assembly rule to Tools~/ci/check_repo.py so the split namespace cannot reappear.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] HappyEyeballsOptions is declared in namespace TurboHTTP.Core (the file stays in Runtime/Core/) and all usages compile
- [ ] Tools~/ci/check_repo.py fails when a type's namespace does not match its owning assembly
- [ ] A check_repo.py self-test or fixture shows the new rule rejecting a mismatched namespace

title: [Transport] HappyEyeballsOptions.Validate accepts attempt delays below the RFC 8305 10 ms floor, including zero
body:
## Summary
Validate only rejects negative FamilyStaggerDelay and AttemptSpacingDelay, so zero is accepted and every due attempt is started in one loop pass. RFC 8305 section 5 forbids starting a connection within 10 ms of the previous attempt. With zero delays and eight addresses, eight SYNs leave in the same millisecond on every connect.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:76`

## Problem
Validate (76-84) only rejects negative FamilyStaggerDelay and AttemptSpacingDelay. BuildSchedule (HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:348-359) uses the values as they are, and RaceAsync starts every attempt whose Due has passed in one loop pass (140-148). RFC 8305 Section 5: 'a subsequent connection MUST NOT be started within 10 milliseconds of the previous attempt'; the recommended minimum is 100 ms.

**Failure scenario.** AttemptSpacingDelay = FamilyStaggerDelay = TimeSpan.Zero with MaxConcurrentAttempts = 8: eight SYNs to eight addresses of one host leave in the same millisecond on every connect, which is the simultaneous-attempt load the RFC forbids.

## Spec reference
RFC 8305 Section 5

## Suggested fix
Clamp both delays to at least 10 ms in the connector (or reject smaller values in Validate) and document the 100 ms recommended minimum and 2 s maximum.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Delays below 10 ms are rejected in Validate or clamped to 10 ms in the connector, consistently
- [ ] The 100 ms recommended minimum and 2 s maximum are documented on the options
- [ ] With zero configured delays, consecutive attempt start times are at least 10 ms apart, covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after

title: [Docs] Public proxy and Happy Eyeballs types (ProxySettings, ProxyBypassMatcher, WithProxy, HappyEyeballsConnector) lack XML documentation
body:
## Summary
ProxySettings, ProxyBypassMatcher, ProxyEnvironmentResolver, the WithProxy/WithoutProxy builder extensions, the proxy metadata key constants and the Happy Eyeballs transport types ship without XML summaries. The security-relevant semantics of AllowPlaintextProxyAuth, AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps and UseEnvironmentVariables (default true, so HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY are honoured with no proxy configured) can only be found by reading the transport source.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:9`

## Problem
No XML summary on: ProxySettings and its members Address, Credentials, UseEnvironmentVariables, AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps, AllowPlaintextProxyAuth, Clone, Validate (ProxySettings.cs:9-65; only BypassList is documented); ProxyBypassMatcher (68) and ProxyEnvironmentResolver with Resolve (225-227); ProxyRequestBuilderExtensions, WithProxy and WithoutProxy (Runtime/Core/ProxyRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:5-23); the RequestMetadataKeys proxy constants; HappyEyeballsConnector (class, Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:14); RawSocketTransport's two option-taking constructors, DispatchAsync and Dispose (RawSocketTransport.cs:47, 55, 141, 2425); TcpConnectionPool.GetConnectionAsync with poolKeyOverride and Dispose (TcpConnectionPool.cs:417, 916); ConnectionLease.Dispose (223). CLAUDE.md section 4 requires XML docs for public API.

**Failure scenario.** The security-relevant semantics of AllowPlaintextProxyAuth (Basic credentials over a cleartext proxy leg), AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps and UseEnvironmentVariables (default true: HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY/NO_PROXY are honoured even with no proxy configured) are only discoverable by reading the transport source; IntelliSense shows nothing for the options a user must set to make an authenticated proxy work.

## Suggested fix
Document the listed members (defaults, the cleartext and credential implications, which paths consult the environment) and turn on CS1591 for the Core and Transport shadow builds so new public members cannot ship undocumented.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every listed public member has an XML summary stating defaults, the cleartext/credential implications and which paths consult the environment
- [ ] CS1591 is enabled for the Core and Transport shadow builds so new undocumented public members fail the build
- [ ] Tools~/ci/check.sh passes with the new warning level and no baseline entries added

title: [Proxy] ProxyEnvironmentResolver re-reads and re-parses HTTP_PROXY/NO_PROXY for every request on every platform
body:
## Summary
UHttpClient.ApplyDefaultMetadata calls ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve for each request. With no configured proxy it calls Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable twice per request, and when a variable is set it also reads NO_PROXY, splits it into a new list, parses the proxy URI and allocates substrings per bypass rule. This runs on developer machines and CI runners on every request and also on iOS/Android where it is useless.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:244`

## Problem
UHttpClient.ApplyDefaultMetadata calls ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve(uri, _options.Proxy) for each request (UHttpClient.cs:753-758). With no configured proxy (the default; UseEnvironmentVariables defaults to true, :28) Resolve calls Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable twice per request (HTTPS_PROXY/https_proxy or HTTP_PROXY/http_proxy, :281-303). When a variable is set it additionally reads NO_PROXY/no_proxy, splits it into a new list (:254-256, :305-320), parses the proxy URI (:251) and allocates a ProxySettings (:270-276) per request. ProxyBypassMatcher.MatchesRule trims and Substrings each rule per request (:93, :105-123, :135, :143). Nothing is cached, although the environment of a running player does not change, and on iOS/Android the variables are not meaningful.

**Failure scenario.** A developer machine or CI runner with HTTPS_PROXY and a long NO_PROXY list: every request pays several getenv calls, a Split, a List, a Uri parse and one or two substrings per bypass rule before dispatch.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the environment once per client (or lazily once per process) into an immutable parsed form with pre-parsed bypass rules, and skip the lookup on iOS/Android players.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The environment is resolved once per client (or once per process) into an immutable form with pre-parsed bypass rules
- [ ] The lookup is skipped on iOS and Android players
- [ ] Steady-state per-request allocations from proxy environment resolution are 0 bytes and 0 getenv calls, measured by a test under Tests/Runtime/Core/ that fails before the fix

title: [Proxy] A proxy taken from HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY cannot authenticate: URL userinfo is ignored and no credentials can be attached
body:
## Summary
ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve builds the environment proxy with Address, BypassList and flags only; Credentials stays null, AllowPlaintextProxyAuth stays false and proxyUri.UserInfo is never read. ProxySettings.Validate rejects Credentials when Address is null, so configuration cannot supply them either. With HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:secret@proxy:3128, every https request fails with a 407 error.

## Location
- `Runtime/Core/ProxySettings.cs:270`

## Problem
ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve builds the environment result with Address, BypassList, UseEnvironmentVariables and AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps only (270-276): Credentials stays null and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth false, and proxyUri.UserInfo is never read. A configured ProxySettings cannot supply them either, because Validate rejects Credentials when Address is null (49-57). EstablishConnectTunnelAsync then fails a 407 with 'credentials were not provided or were rejected' (RawSocketTransport.cs:1491-1509).

**Failure scenario.** HTTPS_PROXY=http://user:secret@proxy.corp:3128 (the form curl, Go, Python and .NET accept): every https request fails with InvalidRequest 'Proxy authentication required (407)'. There is no option that makes the environment proxy usable with authentication short of copying its address into UHttpClientOptions.Proxy.

## Suggested fix
Either read the userinfo into Credentials (still gated by an explicit AllowPlaintextProxyAuth from the configured settings) or allow Credentials/AllowPlaintextProxyAuth on a ProxySettings whose Address comes from the environment, and document which one applies.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An environment proxy with userinfo or explicitly configured credentials authenticates, with the cleartext Basic rule still gated by an explicit AllowPlaintextProxyAuth
- [ ] The chosen behaviour is documented on ProxySettings
- [ ] Credentials from the environment never appear in logs, exceptions or monitors (redacted)
- [ ] A regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ shows a CONNECT through an environment proxy with userinfo completing against a 407 challenge and fails before the fix

title: [Transport] Happy Eyeballs MaxConcurrentAttempts=2 stops the race after two blackholed addresses so later addresses are never dialled
body:
## Summary
RaceAsync starts a scheduled attempt only while fewer than MaxConcurrentAttempts (default 2) are in flight. When the cap is reached it waits on in-flight attempts with no timer, so nothing happens until a connect ends, which for a blackholed SYN is the 10 s connect deadline. A healthy third address is never tried and the request fails with a TCP connect timeout, repeatedly. RFC 8305 section 5 keeps starting attempts on the schedule.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:140`

## Problem
A scheduled attempt starts only while activeTasks.Count < options.MaxConcurrentAttempts (140-142). With the cap reached the loop takes the else branch and awaits Task.WhenAny(activeTasks) with no timer (179-182), so nothing happens until an in-flight connect ends. A blackholed SYN ends only at the OS SYN timeout or the pool connect deadline (10 s, ConnectionPoolOptions.DefaultConnectTimeout), at which point ConnectAsync throws TimeoutException (98-104). RFC 8305 Section 5 keeps starting attempts every Connection Attempt Delay with no in-flight cap. The PromoteIdleFamily comment (230-239) acknowledges the cap's interaction but only fixes the case where one attempt fails fast.

**Failure scenario.** Client on a network with broken IPv6 (SYNs dropped) resolves a host to one AAAA and two A records where the first A is a dead server (round-robin DNS with one node down). Schedule: v6a at 0, v4a at 250 ms, v4b at 375 ms. v6a and v4a both hang, the cap is reached, v4b (healthy) is never dialled, and the request fails with 'TCP connect timed out after 10000ms'. Every retry repeats it because no address state is remembered.

## Spec reference
RFC 8305 Section 5

## Suggested fix
Do not let the cap block progress: when the cap is reached and the next address is due, cancel the oldest in-flight attempt (or raise the default cap to cover the address list within the connect deadline). Add a test with two blackholed and one healthy address under default options.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When the cap is reached and the next address is due, progress continues (oldest attempt cancelled, or the cap raised to cover the address list within the deadline)
- [ ] Two blackholed addresses followed by one healthy address connect to the healthy one within the schedule, under default options
- [ ] The 10 ms inter-attempt floor is kept
- [ ] Covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after, using two blackholed and one healthy address

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-06` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: rfc-compat.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. With activeTasks.Count == MaxConcurrentAttempts (default 2, HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:12) the start loop (:140-142) does nothing and the else branch awaits Task.WhenAny(activeTasks) with no timer (:179-182). For one AAAA plus two A records the schedule is v6a 0 ms, v4a 250 ms, v4b 375 ms (:336-358). Two blackholed attempts end only at the connect deadline (10 s, ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:54), then ct.ThrowIfCancellationRequested (:138) leads to the TimeoutException (:98-104) and UHttpException Timeout (TcpConnectionPool.cs:788-789); v4b is never dialled. PromoteIdleFamily's comment (:230-239) acknowledges that RFC 8305 Section 5 has no cap and only covers a slot freed by a fast failure. HappyEyeballsTests.LargeDnsSet_BoundedConcurrency shows the cap is deliberate, but no test covers two blackholed plus one healthy address. Needs two dead addresses ahead of a healthy one, so it is an edge case, but the request then fails outright with a reachable address unused.

title: [Transport] Happy Eyeballs waits for the stagger delay after every in-flight attempt has already failed
body:
## Summary
When the only active attempt fails, RaceAsync computes the remaining time to the next scheduled attempt and sleeps instead of starting it. For http://localhost with a server bound to 127.0.0.1, the connect to ::1 is refused immediately and the connector idles until 250 ms before dialling IPv4. Every new connection and stale-connection retry pays this delay, and later addresses 125 ms each. RFC 8305 and RFC 6555 implementations start the next attempt when the previous one fails.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:150`

## Problem
RaceAsync starts an attempt only when schedule[scheduleIndex].Due <= started.Elapsed (140-148). When the only active attempt completes with a failure, activeTasks is empty and the loop computes wait = schedule[scheduleIndex].Due - started.Elapsed and awaits Task.Delay(wait) (150-159). BuildSchedule puts the first alternate-family address at FamilyStaggerDelay = 250 ms and later ones 125 ms apart (322-359, HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:10-11). TcpConnectionPool.ResolveDnsAsync returns [::1, 127.0.0.1] for every localhost name (TcpConnectionPool.cs:719-720, LocalhostNames.cs:48-53) and PreferIpv6 is true by default, so ::1 is tried first. PromoteIdleFamily (240-257) only reorders when a slot frees while another attempt is still in flight; it does not cover the empty case. The sequential path (361-382) does move on immediately. No test covers 'first attempt fails fast, next starts at once' (HappyEyeballsInterleaveTests covers only the saturated-slot case).

**Failure scenario.** http://localhost:8080 with a dev server bound to 127.0.0.1 only: connect to ::1 is refused in under a millisecond, then the connector idles until t=250 ms before dialling 127.0.0.1. Every new connection (and every stale-connection retry) pays 250 ms. The same happens on an IPv4-only network when the resolver returns AAAA records and the IPv6 connect fails at once with ENETUNREACH, and 125 ms per additional dead address after that.

## Spec reference
RFC 8305 Section 5

## Suggested fix
When activeTasks becomes empty and addresses remain, start the next scheduled attempt immediately (treat a failure as the end of that attempt's delay, as RFC 6555 and every mainstream implementation do), keeping the 10 ms floor between starts. Add a test with a refusing first family and a virtual clock.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] When no attempt is in flight and addresses remain, the next attempt starts immediately, keeping the 10 ms floor between starts
- [ ] localhost to an IPv4-only listener connects in well under 250 ms (no stagger wait after an immediate refusal)
- [ ] Covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after using a refusing first family and a virtual clock or injected delay

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RaceAsync starts an attempt only when Due <= elapsed (HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:140-148). After the only in-flight attempt fails, activeTasks is empty and the loop awaits Task.Delay(Due - elapsed) (:150-159). BuildSchedule puts the first alternate at FamilyStaggerDelay 250 ms and later attempts 125 ms apart (:322-359; defaults HappyEyeballsOptions.cs:10-13). PromoteIdleFamily (:240-257) only reorders, it never advances a due time. TcpConnectionPool.ResolveDnsAsync returns [::1, 127.0.0.1] for localhost names (TcpConnectionPool.cs:719-720, LocalhostNames.cs:48-53) and PreferIpv6 is true, so a server bound to 127.0.0.1 costs 250 ms per new connection. The sequential path (:361-382) moves on at once. No test asserts the start time after a fast failure (HappyEyeballsInterleaveTests checks order; HappyEyeballsSameFamilyTests has a 5 s bound). The IPv4-only-network case depends on whether the resolver returns AAAA there; the localhost case is deterministic.

Also reported as `net-runtime-06` (merged into this issue).

title: [Transport] Happy Eyeballs closes the socket while a cancelled connect is still pending, relying only on the 1 s abandon gate
body:
## Summary
On cancellation or when a race loser is cancelled, ConnectEndpointAsync abandons the pending Socket.ConnectAsync and disposes the socket at once. AbandonedSocketIo's own comment says the gate is not what keeps a descriptor safe; the stream's handle hold does that, and a socket that never reached a stream has no hold. On IL2CPP iOS, if the selector job is not dispatched, the next connection can be delayed up to 1 s and then get the recycled descriptor behind the stale job. Every Happy Eyeballs win cancels losers this way.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/HappyEyeballsConnector.cs:503`

## Problem
ConnectEndpointAsync abandons a pending Socket.ConnectAsync on cancellation (AbandonableTask.WaitAsync, :498-499, which records it in AbandonedSocketIo) and its catch disposes the socket at once (:503-508). The winner of every race cancels the losers this way (:191-192). AbandonedSocketIo's own comment states that the gate 'is not what keeps a descriptor safe' and that the stream's handle hold does that (Runtime/Core/Internal/AbandonedSocketIo.cs:23-28); a socket that never reached a stream has no hold, and a connect is an I/O-selector job like a receive. If the runtime does not end the abandoned connect within SettleTimeout (1 s), the entry expires and the next socket can be created on the same descriptor number. While such an entry is pending, every new socket in the process (all hosts, WebSocket included) waits in WaitForSettledAsync (:484).

**Failure scenario.** Dual-stack host on a network that blackholes IPv6 (the case Happy Eyeballs exists for), IL2CPP on iOS: v4 wins at about 250 ms, the pending v6 connect is closed; if that job is not dispatched, the next connection in the process is delayed up to 1 s and may then be created on the recycled descriptor behind the stale job. Confirm with a Loop384-style test whose abandoned operation is a blackholed connect.

## Suggested fix
Apply the same lifetime rule as HoldingNetworkStream to connecting sockets: keep the handle until the connect task ended (bounded), instead of closing in the catch; cover it with a device loop before relying on the gate.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A connecting socket's handle is held until its connect task ended (bounded), instead of closing it in the catch, using the same lifetime rule as HoldingNetworkStream
- [ ] The hold is released exactly once on success, failure, cancellation and dispose
- [ ] Covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after using a blackholed-connect loop in the style of the #384 test
- [ ] validated on a device (iOS IL2CPP) and recorded

title: [Transport] NAT64 literal fallback synthesizes 64:ff9b:: addresses for private, link-local and multicast IPv4 literals
body:
## Summary
ConnectWithLiteralFallbackAsync synthesizes an IPv6 address for any IPv4 literal once the direct connect fails with a no-route error, and the synthesizer does not check the IPv4 address. RFC 6052 section 3.1 forbids using the Well-Known Prefix for non-global IPv4 addresses. On an IPv6-only network a request to http://192.168.1.20/ is sent to 64:ff9b::c0a8:114, i.e. to whichever host has that address behind the operator's NAT64, in cleartext.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/Nat64AddressSynthesizer.cs:204`

## Problem
ConnectWithLiteralFallbackAsync (188-216) synthesizes for any IPv4 literal once the direct connect failed with a no-route error and a prefix was discovered (204-214). Synthesize (127-144) has no check on the IPv4 address, and TryExtractPrefix (87-121) returns 64:ff9b::/96 like any other prefix. RFC 6052 Section 3.1: 'The Well-Known Prefix MUST NOT be used to represent non-global IPv4 addresses, such as those defined in [RFC1918]'. Link-local 169.254/16, 0/8, multicast and broadcast literals are synthesized as well. Nat64AddressSynthesizerTests has no private-address case. (#167 tracks the feature, not this restriction.)

**Failure scenario.** On an IPv6-only cellular network an app calls http://192.168.1.20/ (a device on the Wi-Fi it is no longer attached to). The IPv4 connect fails with ENETUNREACH, the transport connects to 64:ff9b::c0a8:114 instead; a translator that does not drop the packet delivers the request (cleartext, with its headers) to whatever host has 192.168.1.20 behind the operator's NAT64.

## Spec reference
RFC 6052 Section 3.1

## Suggested fix
Skip synthesis when the discovered prefix is 64:ff9b::/96 and the literal is not a global unicast address (RFC 1918, 100.64/10, 169.254/16, 127/8, 0/8, multicast, broadcast); never synthesize for link-local, multicast or broadcast under any prefix. Rethrow the original failure in those cases.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Synthesis is skipped under 64:ff9b::/96 for non-global literals (RFC 1918, 100.64/10, 169.254/16, 127/8, 0/8, multicast, broadcast)
- [ ] Link-local, multicast and broadcast literals are never synthesized under any prefix
- [ ] The original connect failure is rethrown in those cases
- [ ] Covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after

title: [Transport] NAT64 prefixes are rediscovered, and the failed IPv4 connect repeated, for every new connection to an IPv4 literal
body:
## Summary
ConnectWithLiteralFallbackAsync first connects to the literal, and only after a no-route failure resolves ipv4only.arpa and connects to synthesized addresses. Nothing caches the prefix or the fact that the network has no IPv4 route. On an IPv6-only carrier network every new connection pays a failed connect plus a DNS query, which is a per-request cost for servers that close after each response.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Connection/Nat64AddressSynthesizer.cs:206`

## Problem
ConnectWithLiteralFallbackAsync first runs the full connect to the literal (:202), and only after it fails with a no-route error resolves ipv4only.arpa (:206 -> DiscoverPrefixesAsync :151-180) and connects to the synthesized addresses (:214). Nothing remembers the discovered prefix (or that the network has no IPv4 route), so every new connection repeats the failed IPv4 attempt and the lookup. TcpConnectionPool calls it for each dial (TcpConnectionPool.cs:649-654).

**Failure scenario.** A game talks to its server by IPv4 literal on an IPv6-only carrier network (the App Review NAT64 case): each new connection pays a failed connect plus a DNS query before the real dial; servers that close after each response make that a per-request cost.

## Suggested fix
Cache the prefix list for a short time (tens of seconds; the resolver API exposes no TTL) keyed to the pool, and try the synthesized addresses first while the cache says the network has no IPv4 route.

## Acceptance criteria

title: [Transport] RawSocketTransport keeps the caller's Http2Options instance and does not null-check poolOptions in the options factory
body:
## Summary
The constructor clones StreamingOptions but passes the caller's Http2Options object to Http2ConnectionManager, which stores it, while two values are read once. Changing the options object after construction partly takes effect on new connections, read from a shared object on connection threads without synchronization, and partly is ignored. The WithOptions factory also dereferences poolOptions without a null check.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:73`

## Problem
Constructor: '_streamingOptions = streamingOptions.Clone()' (73) but '_h2Manager = new Http2ConnectionManager(http2Options, _streamingOptions)' (74) passes the caller's object, which the manager stores as _options (Runtime/Transport/Http2/Http2ConnectionManager.cs:45-50); '_http2ThroughConnectTunnels = http2Options.EnableHttp2ThroughConnectTunnels' (76) and the manager's _maxConnectionsPerOrigin are read once. Http2Options has a Clone() (Runtime/Core/Http2Options.cs:222) that UHttpClient uses, so only direct construction (the documented decorator pattern) is affected. Registration.WithOptions (107-121) reads poolOptions.MaxConnectionsPerHost and seven more properties with no null check, and HttpTransportFactory.CreateWithOptions is public and forwards its arguments unchecked.

**Failure scenario.** var o = new Http2Options(); var t = new RawSocketTransport(null, TlsBackend.Auto, o); o.MaxConcurrentStreams = 1; o.EnableHttp2ThroughConnectTunnels = true; - new connections pick up the first change (read from the shared object on connection threads without synchronisation) and ignore the second. HttpTransportFactory.CreateWithOptions(TlsBackend.Auto, null, new Http2Options(), new StreamingOptions()) throws NullReferenceException from inside the registration lambda instead of ArgumentNullException.

## Suggested fix
Clone http2Options in the constructor like streamingOptions and read every HTTP/2 setting from the clone; validate poolOptions (null -> defaults or ArgumentNullException) in the WithOptions factory.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] RawSocketTransport clones Http2Options in the constructor and reads every HTTP/2 setting from the clone

title: [Transport] Default 10 s first-byte watchdog fails idempotent requests that take longer when the first attempt used a pooled connection
body:
## Summary
GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout arms a 10 s watchdog for every idempotent, replayable request on a reused connection. At expiry the connection is disposed, the stale-connection filter re-sends the request on a new connection, and that retry is armed with the same bound, so it fails at about 20 s. A GET with a 12 to 25 s time to first byte succeeds on a fresh connection but fails with NetworkError on a pooled one, and the server runs it twice.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:344`

## Problem
GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout (344-354) arms the watchdog for every idempotent, replayable request on a reused lease with PlatformConfig.DefaultReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout = 10 s (PlatformConfig.cs:42-44). AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync (1981-2016) disposes the connection at expiry and throws IOException, which the stale filter (665-669) turns into a second send on GetNewConnectionAsync (683). That retry is armed too (retryLease: true, 708-709; #364/#384 stopgap), and its expiry is not retried: the IOException maps to NetworkError (805-806). A server that is simply slow to produce its first byte is indistinguishable from a dead connection, so the request is sent twice and fails after 2 x 10 s although request.Timeout (30 s desktop, 45 s mobile) has not expired. The same request on a non-pooled connection has no watchdog and succeeds. ConnectionPoolOptions.ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout documents the mechanism but not that slow endpoints fail; RetryLeaseFirstByteWatchdogTests asserts the retry's hard failure.

**Failure scenario.** GET long-poll or report endpoint with a 12-25 s time to first byte: the first call on a new connection succeeds; the next call reuses the pooled connection, is aborted at 10 s, re-sent on a new socket (the server now runs it twice) and fails with NetworkError at 20 s. Behaviour depends on whether an idle connection happened to be pooled.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.3.1

## Suggested fix
Do not arm the bound on the fresh retry connection once the #384 descriptor hold is in place (the retry should wait for the request timeout as documented for 'any other fresh connection'), or let the retry's expiry fall back to waiting instead of failing. Document that the bound is a time-to-first-byte limit for idempotent requests and consider a larger default or a liveness probe (SO_KEEPALIVE result, zero-byte read) instead of a response deadline.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The fresh retry connection is not armed with the first-byte bound (it waits for the request timeout), or its expiry falls back to waiting instead of failing
- [ ] A slow endpoint with a time to first byte above 10 s behaves the same whether or not an idle connection was pooled
- [ ] The semantics of the bound (time to first byte on reused connections only) are documented
- [ ] Covered by a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix and passes after, using a pooled connection and a delayed response
- [ ] validated on a device (IL2CPP) and recorded, given the #364/#384 stopgap

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout (:344-354) arms 10 s (PlatformConfig.cs:42-44) for every idempotent replayable request on a reused lease; AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync (:1981-2016) disposes the connection and throws IOException; the filter at :665-669 resends on GetNewConnectionAsync (:683) with retryLease:true (:708-709); the second expiry is thrown from inside the catch handler, so the sibling filter at :730 does not apply and MapDispatchAttemptFailure maps it to NetworkError (:805-806) at about 20 s, below the 30/45 s request timeout. A slow first byte is indistinguishable from a dead connection, and the request is sent twice. Partly weakens the finding: the public doc does state it (ConnectionPoolOptions.cs:146-160: 'The fresh connection of that one retry is bounded by the same time; when it stays silent too, the request fails with no further attempt'), and the retry arming is a recorded stopgap (PR #405, listed under #384's suggested fix, #364). No open issue tracks the cost for slow endpoints (long-poll GET, report endpoints with TTFB above 10 s), which fail only when an idle connection happens to be pooled. The trade-off is deliberate; its cost for legitimate slow responses is real and untracked.

Related: #364, #384.

title: [Transport] Transport control flow depends on string literals: parser message, TLS provider name, ALPN id, IOCP label
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport classifies a stale connection by comparing a FormatException message with the literal "Empty HTTP status line" thrown in Http11ResponseParser. It also selects TLS viability by provider name "SslStream", routes HTTP/2 on the literal "h2" in three places, and derives SaeaPlatformDetection.CloseAbortsPendingIo from a diagnostic label. Rewording a message or renaming a label silently changes retry behaviour or the socket close order on Windows.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:380`

## Problem
IsConnectionClosedBeforeStatusLine (380-387) classifies a stale connection by 'FormatException.Message == "Empty HTTP status line"'; the parser throws that text for string.IsNullOrEmpty(statusLine) (Runtime/Transport/Http1/Http11ResponseParser.cs:273-274), i.e. both for end of stream and for an empty first line, and a parser comment (269-271) is the only thing tying the two files together. 'tlsResult.ProviderName == "SslStream"' decides the Auto-viability marking in two places (TcpConnectionPool.cs:688, RawSocketTransport.cs:1520). 'NegotiatedAlpnProtocol == "h2"' routes to HTTP/2 in three places (622, 686, 1420) while AlpnProtocols holds the offered ids. SaeaPlatformDetection.CloseAbortsPendingIo is 'CompletionModelName == "IOCP"' (Runtime/Transport/Tcp/SaeaPlatformDetection.cs:72), so a diagnostics label (with an 'unknown' fallback at 119) selects the socket close order for SaeaSocketChannel and SocketHandleHold; the doc comment at 43-45 has to warn that the label must not be renamed.

**Failure scenario.** Rewording the parser message (or localising it, or a server that sends a bare CRLF before the status line on a reused connection) changes retry behaviour: a first-line protocol error is treated as 'server closed the idle connection' and an idempotent request is replayed, or a real idle close stops being retried. Renaming the IOCP label silently switches Windows to the hold-the-descriptor close order.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.3.1

## Suggested fix
Throw a dedicated internal exception type (or return a result flag) for 'EOF before the first status-line byte', compare providers by identity or an enum on TlsResult, define the 'h2' id once in AlpnProtocols, and make CloseAbortsPendingIo a bool computed from the platform defines with the label derived from it.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Stale-connection classification uses a dedicated exception type or result flag, not an exception message comparison
- [ ] TLS provider viability and HTTP/2 routing use an enum/identity and a single AlpnProtocols constant, not string literals
- [ ] SaeaPlatformDetection.CloseAbortsPendingIo is a bool computed from platform defines; the label is derived from it
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix (changing the parser message text does not change retry classification)

title: [Transport] HTTP/1.1 dispatch allocates three CTSs, two timers, key strings and seven async frames per reused-connection request
body:
## Summary
Each HTTP/1.1 request on a keep-alive connection creates a linked CTS with timer, a watchdog CTS with its own timer, interpolated pool and HTTP/2 key strings, boxed state values, five TimelineEvent objects and seven nested async methods. Issue #120 covers body transport, parser strings and HTTP/2 lists but not this dispatch layer. Clients that poll or fetch many small resources pay roughly 20-30 small objects per request, which shows up as GC pressure on Mono and IL2CPP.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:439`

## Problem
Per request, before any body work: a linked CTS plus CancelAfter timer (:439-440); for every https request a key string built with $"{host}:{port}" (boxed int, string.Format) in Http2ConnectionManager.GetIfExists (:586 -> Http2ConnectionManager.cs:76); another interpolated key in TcpConnectionPool.BuildConnectionKey (TcpConnectionPool.cs:276, called at :451) and a ConnectionLease; Http11RequestWriteState (:649); a dispose-on-cancel registration (:1776); for an idempotent request on a reused connection a BufferedStreamReader created outside the parser (:1949) plus a watchdog CTS with its own timer, a second linked CTS and another registration (:1987-1992); boxing in context.SetState(..., true) and SetState(..., long) (:154, :2405-2407); a TimelineEvent object per RecordEvent, five on the plain path (TransportStart, TransportConnecting, TransportSending, TransportReceiving, TransportComplete; RequestContext.cs:114-116). The call chain is seven nested async Task methods that all complete asynchronously (DispatchAsync, DispatchCoreAsync, DispatchAttemptAsync, DispatchOnLeaseAsync, SendOnLeaseAsync, AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync, EmitParsedResponseHeadAsync), each boxing its state machine and allocating a Task. #120 covers the body transport, parser strings and HTTP/2 lists, not this dispatch layer.

**Failure scenario.** A client that polls or fetches many small resources over keep-alive HTTP/1.1 (the pool's best case) pays on every request for two timer insertions/removals and roughly 20-30 small objects in the dispatch layer alone, which shows up as GC pressure on Mono/IL2CPP (Boehm) at a few hundred requests per second or in a per-frame request pattern.

## Suggested fix
Fold the first-byte bound into the request CTS (one timer re-armed, or a deadline checked by the existing dispose-on-cancel registration) instead of two more sources; cache the pool/h2 keys per (host, port, secure) or key the dictionaries with a struct; flatten the pass-through async layers (return the inner Task where nothing happens after the await); store the state flags without boxing.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Dispatch layer allocations per reused-connection HTTP/1.1 GET are measured before and after with the frame/alloc counter and reduced (target: at most one CTS and one timer per request, no per-request key string allocation)
- [ ] Pool and HTTP/2 keys are cached or struct-keyed per (host, port, secure); state flags are stored without boxing
- [ ] Pass-through async layers return the inner Task where nothing follows the await
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix asserting the allocation or object-count bound

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-runtime-09` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: performance.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: The listed allocations exist: linked CTS + CancelAfter per request (RawSocketTransport.cs:439-440); interpolated key with a boxed int in Http2ConnectionManager.GetIfExists (Http2ConnectionManager.cs:76, called at RawSocketTransport.cs:586 for every https request) and in BuildConnectionKey (TcpConnectionPool.cs:276, called :451); ConnectionLease (:523); Http11RequestWriteState (:649); dispose-on-cancel registration (:1776); on an armed first-byte path a second CTS with timer, a linked CTS and another registration (:1987-1992); SetState(string, object) boxes the bool and the long (RequestContext.cs:136, RawSocketTransport.cs:154 and :2405-2407); RecordEvent allocates a TimelineEvent class instance each call (RequestContext.cs:13, :116). The async chain is DispatchAsync -> DispatchCoreAsync -> DispatchAttemptAsync -> DispatchOnLeaseAsync -> SendOnLeaseAsync (+ AwaitFirstResponseByteAsync, EmitParsedResponseHeadAsync), all async Task. One detail is off: the BufferedStreamReader at :1949 is not extra, the unarmed path creates one inside ParseHeadAsync. #120 (body transport, parser strings, H2 lists) does not cover the dispatch layer. Lowered to low: this is a fixed per-request cost of a few hundred bytes next to the 2-5 KB per response that #120 already tracks, not a per-read or per-frame cost, and the dispatch layer was never one of the allocation-free paths.

title: [Transport] Out-of-range request timeout or disposed transport escapes DispatchAsync as a raw exception, not UHttpException
body:
## Summary
DispatchCoreAsync passes request.Timeout to CancelAfter, which throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for values below -1 ms or above int.MaxValue ms, and UHttpRequest.WithTimeout does not validate. DispatchAsync catches only UHttpException and OperationCanceledException, so this and the ObjectDisposedException fault the task without OnResponseError. This violates the error model and leaves retry and metrics interceptors without a terminal callback.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:440`

## Problem
DispatchCoreAsync calls timeoutCts.CancelAfter(request.Timeout) (439-440); UHttpRequest.WithTimeout stores any TimeSpan without validation (UHttpRequest.cs:330-336). CancelAfter throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a value below -1 ms or above int.MaxValue ms. DispatchAsync catches only UHttpException and OperationCanceledException (173-187), so that exception, and the ObjectDisposedException at 435-436, fault the dispatch task without handler.OnResponseError. CLAUDE.md section 3 and the MapDispatchAttemptFailure summary (759-766) state that failures are UHttpException(UHttpError).

**Failure scenario.** request.WithTimeout(TimeSpan.MaxValue) to mean 'no timeout' (or TimeSpan.FromDays(30)): the send fails with ArgumentOutOfRangeException from inside the transport after OnRequestStart already ran; interceptors that expect OnResponseError or a UHttpException (retry, metrics) never see a terminal callback.

## Suggested fix
Validate the timeout at the start of DispatchCoreAsync (map invalid values to UHttpErrorType.InvalidRequest, treat values above the timer range as infinite) and wrap the remaining pre-dispatch faults the same way.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] WithTimeout(TimeSpan.MaxValue) or a value above the timer range is treated as an infinite timeout
- [ ] Invalid timeouts (below -1 ms other than infinite) and a disposed transport surface as UHttpException with UHttpErrorType.InvalidRequest (or the documented type) and handler.OnResponseError is invoked
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix covering MaxValue, FromDays(30) and a negative value

title: [Transport] Link-local IPv6 literal URLs lose their zone id in the lookup host, so the connect fails
body:
## Summary
DispatchCoreAsync derives the DNS/connect host from WireHost.LookupHost, which returns Uri.Host without the scope id for IPv6 literals. The pool then resolves an address with ScopeId 0, so a link-local URL such as http://[fe80::1%25en0]:8080/ cannot be connected although the URL is valid. Dropping the zone is correct for Host and :authority but not for the connect.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:477`

## Problem
DispatchCoreAsync takes the DNS/connect host from WireHost.LookupHost(request.Uri, wireHost) (477), which for an IPv6 literal returns StripBrackets(uri.Host) (WireHost.cs:86-91). Uri.Host omits the scope id on .NET (DnsSafeHost carries it), and the pool hands that string to Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync (TcpConnectionPool.cs:724), which yields an IPAddress with ScopeId 0. Removing the zone is right for the wire host (RFC 3986 IP-literal, RFC 6874), but the connect needs it. Whether Unity Mono's Uri.Host keeps the zone decides the outcome; the WireHost comments record that Mono's Host has differed from .NET before.

**Failure scenario.** http://[fe80::1c2b:3aff:fe4d:5e6f%25en0]:8080/ for a device discovered on the local link: the connect is attempted to fe80::... with no scope and fails with EINVAL/no route, although the URL is valid and the Host header is correctly zone-free.

## Spec reference
RFC 6874 Section 2

## Suggested fix
Derive the lookup host for IPv6 literals from Uri.DnsSafeHost (zone kept, brackets removed) while keeping the zone-free form for Host, :authority, CONNECT and pool keys. Confirm with a link-local address on a Unity 2021.3 Mono and IL2CPP player.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The connect host for IPv6 literals keeps the zone id (Uri.DnsSafeHost without brackets) while Host, :authority, CONNECT and pool keys stay zone-free
- [ ] A link-local address with a zone connects to the right interface
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix for LookupHost vs wire host with a zone id
- [ ] Behaviour on Unity 2021.3 Mono and IL2CPP players validated on a device and recorded

title: [Transport] RawSocketTransport is a 2434-line class with the HTTP/2 hand-off copy-pasted four times and already diverged
body:
## Summary
RawSocketTransport holds factory registration, dispatch and error mapping, HTTP/2 routing, the HTTP/1.1 stale retry, the whole proxy feature, the first-byte watchdog and the Expect: 100-continue state machine. The HTTP/2 hand-off and the committed-non-replayable-body clause each exist four times, and two copies already lack the extra-dial fallback. The two filtered catch clauses at 665/730 and 1106/1183 are safe on IL2CPP only because their filters are mutually exclusive.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:622`

## Problem
One sealed class holds: factory registration and capability probing (79-139), dispatch entry and the error-model mapping (141-258, 746-836), HTTP/2 routing with extra-dial claims (583-646, 1029-1045), the HTTP/1.1 stale-retry policy (284-395, 648-739), the whole proxy feature - forward proxy, CONNECT tunnel, Basic 407 handling, tunnel pool keys, lease rebinding (838-1296, 1310-1581, about 730 lines), the first-byte watchdog (1969-2016) and the Expect: 100-continue state machine (2018-2364, about 350 lines). The sequence 'lease.TransferOwnership(); GetOrCreateAsync; lease = null; DispatchOnH2ConnectionAsync' exists four times: 622-644 and 964-992 wrap GetOrCreateAsync in a try/catch that calls FallBackAfterFailedExtraDial and call ReleaseExtraDial afterwards; the two stale-retry copies 686-696 and 1133-1150 have neither. The 'ShouldSurfaceCommittedNonReplayableBodyFailure -> CreateCommittedNonReplayableBodyFailure' clause exists four times (715-723, 730-738, 1168-1176, 1183-1191). The comment at 510-511 says one filtered clause, not two, because IL2CPP nests the clauses of a filtered try (#320), yet the try at 650 and the try at 1091 each carry two filtered clauses (665+730, 1106+1183); they are only safe because the two filters happen to be mutually exclusive on request.Content.Replayability.

**Failure scenario.** A change to one hand-off or retry copy (as already happened with the #238 extra-dial fallback and the #47 fresh-socket retry, see net-design-02) is not applied to its siblings, and nothing in the type system or tests points at the other three places. A future edit that makes the two filters of 665/730 overlap re-introduces the #320 IL2CPP mis-catch with no compiler or analyzer signal.

## Suggested fix
Split by responsibility: a ProxyConnector (forward/CONNECT/auth, owns tunnel pool keys), an Http11Exchange (send, Expect-continue, first-byte watchdog, stale retry as one method parameterised by a lease factory), an H2 hand-off helper used by all four sites, and keep RawSocketTransport as the router plus error mapping. Make the stale retry one implementation that takes 'acquire fresh lease' as a delegate so direct and proxy paths cannot diverge.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Proxy handling, HTTP/1.1 exchange (send, Expect-continue, watchdog, stale retry) and the HTTP/2 hand-off are extracted so each sequence exists once
- [ ] Stale retry is a single implementation parameterised by an acquire-fresh-lease delegate used by direct and proxy paths
- [ ] Filtered try blocks keep a single filtered clause per try (see #320) with a comment or analyzer note
- [ ] Existing transport tests pass unchanged; add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix for the previously diverged copies

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-design-01` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: File is 2434 lines and holds every responsibility listed. The h2 hand-off exists four times: RawSocketTransport.cs:622-644 and :964-992 with the FallBackAfterFailedExtraDial catch, :686-696 and :1133-1150 without. That difference is not itself a bug: both stale-retry copies run after the claim was released (:646, :994), so there is nothing to fall back to; the finding stands as duplication, not as a defect at those two sites. The committed-non-replayable clause exists four times (:715-723, :730-738, :1168-1176, :1183-1191), and the two inner copies are dead code: the enclosing clause is entered only when CanRetryHttp11RequestAfterTransportFailure passed, i.e. Replayability != NonReplayable (:288-289), while the inner filter requires NonReplayable (:372). The tries at :650 and :1091 each carry two filtered clauses (:665+:730, :1106+:1183) although the comments at :510-511 and :748-751 state that IL2CPP lets a later clause catch what an earlier clause threw (#320); they are safe only because the two filters are mutually exclusive on Replayability, and nothing enforces that. #182 tracks oversized files in Core only (PluginContext, MainThreadDispatcher, UHttpClient, DecompressionHandler), not this one.

title: [Transport] Missing TLS provider maps to retryable NetworkError or Unknown after TCP connect instead of a configuration error
body:
## Summary
TlsProviderSelector throws PlatformNotSupportedException or InvalidOperationException (BouncyCastle not compiled), but the provider is resolved only after DNS and the TCP connect. MapDispatchAttemptFailure has no case for either, so the first becomes a retryable NetworkError with the text "Unsupported HTTP response" and the second becomes Unknown. Users with TlsBackend.BouncyCastle without TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE open and close a TCP connection per request and the Retry interceptor replays a permanent configuration error.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:814`

## Problem
TlsProviderSelector.GetAutoProvider throws PlatformNotSupportedException when SslStream is unavailable (Runtime/Transport/Tls/TlsProviderSelector.cs:224) and SslStreamTlsProvider throws it for an offer it cannot negotiate (SslStreamTlsProvider.cs:294, 410); GetBouncyCastleProvider throws InvalidOperationException when the opt-in assembly is not compiled (TlsProviderSelector.cs:90). TcpConnectionPool.CreateConnectionAsync resolves the provider only after DNS and the TCP connect succeeded (649-683) and rethrows the raw exception (696-705). MapDispatchAttemptFailure has no case for either: PlatformNotSupportedException derives from NotSupportedException and falls into 'case NotSupportedException' (814-818), producing UHttpErrorType.NetworkError with the text 'Unsupported HTTP response: ...'; InvalidOperationException reaches the default branch (827-828) as UHttpErrorType.Unknown. UHttpError.IsRetryable returns true for NetworkError (Runtime/Core/UHttpError.cs:72-74). RawSocketTransportFailureMappingTests has no row for either exception.

**Failure scenario.** A client created with TlsBackend.BouncyCastle in a project that did not define TURBOHTTP_BOUNCYCASTLE constructs fine; every https request then resolves DNS, opens and closes a TCP connection to the server and fails with Unknown. With TlsBackend.Auto on a runtime without a usable SslStream, the permanent platform error is labelled as a malformed server response and the Retry interceptor replays it with backoff as if it were a network fault.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the provider before dialling (first statement of CreateConnectionAsync / EstablishConnectTunnelAsync) and map PlatformNotSupportedException and the missing-provider case to a non-retryable configuration error (InvalidRequest or a dedicated type) with their own message; add both rows to RawSocketTransportFailureMappingTests.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The TLS provider is resolved before DNS and dialling in CreateConnectionAsync and EstablishConnectTunnelAsync
- [ ] PlatformNotSupportedException and the missing-provider case map to a non-retryable error (InvalidRequest or a dedicated type) with a message naming the cause
- [ ] UHttpError.IsRetryable is false for both cases

title: [Proxy] Request-level ProxySettings are not validated: an https:// proxy address is contacted in cleartext on port 80
body:
## Summary
ProxySettings.Validate runs only for client-level options through ProxyEnvironmentResolver, while WithProxy stores the settings unvalidated. DispatchViaProxyAsync computes port 80 when the address uses the default port, so https://secure-proxy.corp is contacted in cleartext on port 80, https://host:8443 gets cleartext HTTP, and socks5:// is treated as an HTTP proxy. The CONNECT line and Basic Proxy-Authorization are then sent unencrypted although the caller believes the proxy leg is TLS.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:861`

## Problem
ProxySettings.Validate (ProxySettings.cs:47-65) rejects non-http schemes, but it is only called from ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve for UHttpClientOptions.Proxy (ProxySettings.cs:232). WithProxy (ProxyRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:7-15) stores a clone without validating, and UHttpClient skips resolution when the key is present (UHttpClient.cs:753-754). DispatchViaProxyAsync only checks Address != null (852-857), then computes proxyPort = proxy.Address.IsDefaultPort ? 80 : proxy.Address.Port (861-863) and always leases with secure: false (1218-1223). For https://proxy.example the default port is 443, so IsDefaultPort is true and the transport connects to proxy.example:80 in cleartext; for https://proxy.example:8443 it speaks cleartext HTTP to a TLS port; socks5:// is treated as an HTTP proxy. A ProxySettings with Address null fails with 'Proxy address is required' instead of meaning 'no proxy'. No test calls WithProxy.

**Failure scenario.** request.WithProxy(new ProxySettings { Address = new Uri("https://secure-proxy.corp"), Credentials = ..., AllowPlaintextProxyAuth = true }): the caller believes the proxy leg is TLS; the CONNECT line with the target host and, after a Basic challenge, Proxy-Authorization are sent unencrypted to secure-proxy.corp:80 (on desktop, where AllowCleartext defaults to true).

## Suggested fix
Validate at the transport boundary: reject a proxy whose scheme is not http with InvalidRequest (the message must not echo the URI), treat Address == null as no proxy, and use Address.Port directly. Calling Validate() in WithProxy as well gives the caller the error at the call site.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A proxy whose scheme is not http is rejected at the transport boundary with UHttpErrorType.InvalidRequest; the message does not echo the URI
- [ ] ProxySettings with Address == null means no proxy; the port is taken from Address.Port
- [ ] WithProxy validates the settings so the error appears at the call site
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix for https://, socks5:// and null address through request.WithProxy

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-04` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ProxySettings.Validate (ProxySettings.cs:47-65) is called only by ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve (:232). WithProxy stores proxySettings?.Clone() unvalidated (ProxyRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:7-15) and UHttpClient skips Resolve when the key exists (UHttpClient.cs:753-754). DispatchViaProxyAsync checks only Address != null (:852-857), uses IsDefaultPort ? 80 : Port (:861-863), so https://proxy.example becomes proxy.example:80, and always leases secure:false (:1218-1223). A ProxySettings with Address null fails with 'Proxy address is required' (transport treats proxy != null as proxied, :565). No test calls WithProxy (rg over Tests, Samples~, Documentation~: none). Limits on impact: the cleartext policy still applies to the proxy host (:495-501), so a mobile default rejects it; Proxy-Authorization goes out only after a Basic 407 and only with AllowPlaintextProxyAuth = true, so the credential exposure needs that opt-in plus something answering 407 on the cleartext port (an on-path attacker can). In most cases the result is a confusing connect failure, not a leak.

title: [Proxy] Forward-proxy Basic auth is never sent preemptively: every request is sent twice, non-replayable uploads fail with 407
body:
## Summary
DispatchViaProxyAsync sends every forwarded request without credentials, answers a Basic 407 only when the body is replayable, and does not remember that the proxy already challenged. A replayable 5 MB POST is uploaded twice and a non-seekable stream body always ends with 407 even though credentials and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth are set. RFC 7617 Section 2.2 allows preemptive credentials within the protection space.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:886`

## Problem
DispatchViaProxyAsync builds every forwarded request with includeCredentials: false (889), intercepts a Basic 407 only when the body is replayable (886-888), and then sends it again with credentials (909-925). Nothing remembers that this proxy already issued a Basic challenge, so the next request starts without credentials again. RFC 7617 Section 2.2 allows a client to send Basic credentials preemptively within a protection space once challenged (for a proxy the protection space is the proxy). RawSocketTransportProxy407Tests.ForwardProxy_NonReplayableBody_Returns407WithoutRetry asserts the non-replayable outcome.

**Failure scenario.** http:// uploads through an authenticating forward proxy: a POST with a replayable 5 MB body is uploaded in full twice (first copy rejected with 407); a POST whose body is a non-seekable stream always ends with 407 delivered to the caller and can never succeed, although the credentials are configured and AllowPlaintextProxyAuth is set.

## Spec reference
RFC 7617 Section 2.2

## Suggested fix
Record, per proxy endpoint and credential, that a Basic challenge was answered successfully and send Proxy-Authorization preemptively on later forwarded requests to that proxy (still only with AllowPlaintextProxyAuth); invalidate the record on a 407.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a Basic challenge was answered successfully, later forwarded requests to the same proxy and credential send Proxy-Authorization preemptively (only with AllowPlaintextProxyAuth)
- [ ] The record is invalidated on a 407
- [ ] A non-replayable body succeeds on the second and later requests through an authenticating proxy
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix in Tests/Runtime/Transport/ (extending RawSocketTransportProxy407Tests)

title: [Proxy] HTTP/1.1 stale-connection retry has a direct and a proxy copy; the proxy copy lacks fresh-socket retry and watchdog
body:
## Summary
DispatchProxyHttp11WithRetryAsync passes no first-byte timeout to DispatchOnLeaseAsync and retries through GetConnectionAsync, which takes the next idle connection. The direct path arms ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout and retries on a new socket (#47). Behind an http:// proxy with several idle connections dropped by a NAT, a silent connection waits for the full request timeout and a faulting one retries on a second dead connection and fails.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1093`

## Problem
Direct copy (648-729): DispatchOnLeaseAsync is called with firstByteTimeout: GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout(lease, request) (652-659); the retry leases through _pool.GetNewConnectionAsync (683, skipIdle: true, TcpConnectionPool.cs:434-438) and arms the watchdog again with retryLease: true (708-709). Proxy copy (DispatchProxyHttp11WithRetryAsync 1054-1197): DispatchOnLeaseAsync is called at 1093-1100 and 1155-1162 with the positional interceptBasicProxyChallenge only, so firstByteTimeout is default(TimeSpan) and SendOnLeaseAsync skips the watchdog (1939); the retry leases through AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync (1121) -> _pool.GetConnectionAsync(..., poolKeyOverride, ct) (1218-1223) with skipIdle: false, i.e. the next idle connection. ConnectionPoolOptions.ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout documents the behaviour without a proxy exception. No test under Tests/Runtime covers a silent or doubly-stale reused proxy connection (rg FirstByte finds only the direct-path fixtures).

**Failure scenario.** Editor or desktop player behind an http:// proxy, two idle keep-alive connections to the proxy (or two idle tunnels to one origin), NAT drops both. An idempotent GET on the first one: if it is silent the request waits for the full request timeout (no 10 s watchdog); if it faults, the single retry dequeues the second dead idle connection and the request fails with NetworkError, where the direct path would have recovered on a new socket.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.3.1

## Suggested fix
Fold both copies into one retry routine that takes the 'new connection' lease factory as a parameter (for proxies: GetNewConnectionAsync on the proxy key followed by the tunnel setup) and always passes the first-byte bound.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Direct and proxy paths use one stale-retry routine that takes the new-connection lease factory as a parameter
- [ ] The proxy path arms the same first-byte bound and retries on a new connection (GetNewConnectionAsync on the proxy key, then tunnel setup)
- [ ] ConnectionPoolOptions.ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout behaves the same with and without a proxy
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix for a silent and a doubly-stale reused proxy connection

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-design-02` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: code-smell.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. Direct path: first attempt passes firstByteTimeout: GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout(lease, request) (RawSocketTransport.cs:652-659), the retry leases with _pool.GetNewConnectionAsync (:683, skipIdle: true, TcpConnectionPool.cs:434-438) and arms the watchdog again (:708-709). Proxy path: DispatchProxyHttp11WithRetryAsync calls DispatchOnLeaseAsync with seven positional arguments (:1093-1100, :1155-1162), the seventh being interceptBasicProxyChallenge, so firstByteTimeout stays default(TimeSpan) (signature :1765-1773) and SendOnLeaseAsync takes the unguarded branch (:1939-1946). The retry leases through AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync (:1121) -> _pool.GetConnectionAsync(..., poolKeyOverride, ct) (:1218-1223), which is skipIdle: false (TcpConnectionPool.cs:417-425), so it can dequeue the next idle proxy connection or tunnel. Result: a silent reused proxy connection waits for the full request timeout, and a faulting one can retry onto a second dead idle one. No guard found, and no test covers it (rg FirstByte finds only Tests/Runtime/Transport/Http1 fixtures, none under Tests/Runtime/Proxy). #364 covers the direct-path retry only. RFC 9112 Section 9.3.1 makes the retry optional, so this is a robustness gap against the documented ReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout behaviour, not a protocol violation.

Also reported as `http1-design-01` (merged into this issue).

Related: #364, #448, [[R11-net-protocol-07]], [[R11-net-design-01]].

title: [Proxy] Proxy paths lack the first-byte watchdog and retry on the next idle connection instead of a new socket
body:
## Summary
Forward-proxy and CONNECT-tunnel dispatch call DispatchOnLeaseAsync without a first-byte timeout and retry through the pool's idle queue, so a NAT that drops all idle connections defeats the single retry. If the dead connections are silent, an idempotent GET hangs until the request timeout. Issue #364 tracks only the direct path.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1121`

## Problem
The direct path arms GetReusedConnectionFirstByteTimeout (659) and retries on _pool.GetNewConnectionAsync (683) with the comment 'A newly connected socket, not the next idle one: a NAT drop kills every idle connection to the host at once (#47)'. DispatchProxyHttp11WithRetryAsync calls DispatchOnLeaseAsync without firstByteTimeout (1093-1100, 1155-1162; default(TimeSpan) disables it at 1939), and its retry leases through AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync (1121-1131), which calls _pool.GetConnectionAsync (1218-1223), i.e. the idle queue first. A second idle connection is marked IsReused but the retry block has no further stale handling, so its failure is final. Open issue #364 tracks only the direct path.

**Failure scenario.** Three idle keep-alive connections to a forward proxy (or three idle CONNECT tunnels to one origin) are dropped by a NAT/firewall without FIN. An idempotent GET fails on the first (reset on read), the retry dequeues the second dead one and fails with NetworkError although a fresh connection would work. If the dead connections are silent instead of reset, the GET hangs until the request timeout because no first-byte bound is armed.

## Spec reference
RFC 9112 Section 9.3.1

## Suggested fix
Give AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync a skipIdle mode for the retry (GetNewConnectionAsync with the pool key override) and pass the same first-byte bound as the direct path, so the proxy and direct paths share one stale-connection policy.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync has a skip-idle mode used by the retry (GetNewConnectionAsync with the pool key override)
- [ ] The proxy path passes the same first-byte bound as the direct path
- [ ] An idempotent GET over a proxy with several dead idle connections succeeds on a new connection or fails within the first-byte bound
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix in Tests/Runtime/Transport/

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: protocol-impl.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. DispatchProxyHttp11WithRetryAsync calls DispatchOnLeaseAsync without firstByteTimeout at :1093-1100 and :1155-1162; the parameter defaults to default(TimeSpan) (:1773), which SendOnLeaseAsync treats as not armed (:1939). Its retry leases through AcquirePreparedProxyLeaseAsync (:1121-1131), which calls _pool.GetConnectionAsync (:1218-1223, skipIdle false, TcpConnectionPool.cs:424), i.e. the idle queue first, while the direct path uses GetNewConnectionAsync with the #47 comment (:680-683). A second idle connection has IsReused = true but the retry block has no further stale filter (:1168-1176 handles only the non-replayable case). #364 and the #47 work cover the direct path only. Partial mitigation: the pool's IsAlive check on dequeue (TcpConnectionPool.cs:510) drops idle sockets that already received RST/FIN, so the 'second dead one' case needs silently dropped connections; with those, the missing first-byte bound means the request waits for the full request timeout, the exact #47 symptom, on both the forward-proxy and the CONNECT-tunnel HTTP/1.1 paths.

Also reported as `net-runtime-11` (merged into this issue).

Related: #364, [[R11-net-design-02]].

title: [Proxy] Proxy selection and BypassList are decided once for the first URI and reused for redirect targets
body:
## Summary
ResolveProxySettings returns whatever ProxySettings is in request metadata and never evaluates ProxyBypassMatcher or the request scheme. ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve runs only when the request is created, and RedirectInterceptor copies the metadata to follow-up requests, so a redirect to a NO_PROXY host still goes through the proxy. A redirect from http to https is tunnelled through HTTP_PROXY even when AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps is false, and a request-level WithProxy never applies its BypassList.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1310`

## Problem
ResolveProxySettings (1310-1326) returns whatever ProxySettings object is in request metadata; it never calls ProxyBypassMatcher or looks at the request URI or scheme. The only caller of ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve is UHttpClient.ApplyDefaultMetadata (UHttpClient.cs:753-758), which runs when the request is created. RedirectInterceptor builds each follow-up request from CloneMetadata(source.Metadata) (RedirectInterceptor.cs:140-141), so the follow-up carries the first hop's ProxySettings (or its absence) to a different host and scheme. A request-level WithProxy(settings) (ProxyRequestBuilderExtensions.cs:7-15) skips resolution entirely, so its BypassList is dead data.

**Failure scenario.** (a) NO_PROXY=.corp.internal, HTTP_PROXY set: GET http://public.example answers 302 to http://wiki.corp.internal/...; the follow-up, with its path, query and cookies, is sent to the external proxy although the host is on the bypass list. (b) Only HTTP_PROXY is set and AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps is false: http://a.example redirects to https://a.example and the https hop is CONNECT-tunneled through HTTP_PROXY, which the configuration forbids. (c) The first URI was bypassed, the redirect target is not: the follow-up goes direct instead of through the proxy.

## Suggested fix
Resolve the proxy per dispatch against the URI actually being sent: either have the transport apply BypassList/scheme rules to request.Uri in ResolveProxySettings, or carry the unresolved configuration in metadata and have the redirect hop re-run ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve. Add redirect tests across a bypass boundary and across http->https with only HTTP_PROXY set.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The proxy decision is made per dispatch against the URI actually sent (BypassList and scheme rules), either in the transport or by re-running the resolver on redirect hops
- [ ] Request-level WithProxy honours its BypassList
- [ ] A redirect across a bypass boundary and an http to https redirect with only HTTP_PROXY set behave per configuration
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix for the redirect cases (a)-(c) of the finding

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-protocol-03` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: security.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. ProxyEnvironmentResolver.Resolve is called only from UHttpClient.ApplyDefaultMetadata (UHttpClient.cs:753-758) with the first URI; bypass and scheme rules live only there (ProxySettings.cs:234-258, :281-303). RawSocketTransport.ResolveProxySettings (:1310-1326) returns the metadata object and never looks at request.Uri or BypassList (no ProxyBypassMatcher reference anywhere in Runtime/Transport). RedirectInterceptor.BuildRedirectRequest copies the metadata dictionary (RedirectInterceptor.cs:140-141, :210-216) and dispatches the follow-up through next, not through UHttpClient, so the first hop's decision (proxy object, or its absence) applies to every redirect target. All three scenarios hold: bypass-listed redirect target sent to the proxy, https hop tunneled through HTTP_PROXY with AllowHttpProxyFallbackForHttps false, and a non-bypassed target sent direct after a bypassed first hop. No redirect test in Tests/Runtime/Proxy and no proxy handling in RedirectHandler.cs.

Also reported as `core-design-03`, `mw-protocol-10`, `net-design-03` (merged into this issue).

title: [Proxy] A caller-supplied Proxy-Authorization header is stripped on proxied paths but sent to the origin on direct connections
body:
## Summary
The proxy forward and tunnel preparation remove Proxy-Authorization, but the direct branch of DispatchAttemptAsync sends request headers as they are over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2. When the target is on the bypass list, NO_PROXY matches or no proxy is configured, the proxy credential reaches the origin server and a same-origin redirect target. This violates the rule that Proxy-Authorization stays on the proxy hop.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1342`

## Problem
PrepareHttpProxyForwardRequest (1341-1342) and PrepareHttpsProxyTunnelRequest (1359-1360) call headers.Remove("Proxy-Authorization"); the direct branch of DispatchAttemptAsync (580-745) dispatches the request headers as they are, over HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 (HpackEncoder only marks the field never-indexed, HpackEncoder.cs:259). The only other removal is on a cross-origin redirect hop (RedirectInterceptor.cs:136). So the one place the header can reach the wire is a hop that has no proxy. CLAUDE.md section 3: Proxy-Authorization stays on the proxy hop.

**Failure scenario.** An app sets Proxy-Authorization on its requests (a pattern carried over from other HTTP clients). When the target is on the bypass list, NO_PROXY matches, or no proxy is configured on this machine, the proxy credential is delivered to the origin server (and to a same-origin redirect target).

## Spec reference
RFC 9110 Section 11.7.2

## Suggested fix
Strip Proxy-Authorization in the direct path as well (it is meaningful only to a proxy), or reject it as a transport-owned field with InvalidRequest.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The direct path strips Proxy-Authorization before serialising (HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2), or rejects it with InvalidRequest
- [ ] Proxied paths keep their current behaviour
- [ ] Add a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ that fails before the fix asserting the header never appears on the wire for direct HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 requests

title: [Proxy] Every proxied request clones headers and metadata and makes three request copies, also on HTTP/2 tunnel reuse
body:
## Summary
PrepareHttpsProxyTunnelRequest and PrepareHttpProxyForwardRequest build a new metadata dictionary, clone HttpHeaders and chain several request copies for every proxied request, twice on a Basic 407 retry, plus rebuild tunnel pool keys from strings with boxed ports. A desktop build behind a corporate proxy allocates this before any I/O on top of the direct-path cost.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/RawSocketTransport.cs:1356`

## Problem
PrepareHttpsProxyTunnelRequest and PrepareHttpProxyForwardRequest each build a new Dictionary from the request metadata (CloneMetadataWith :1570-1581), clone HttpHeaders (:1341, :1359) and chain CopyWithSharedContent().WithHeaders().WithMetadata() (:1350-1353, :1362-1365). They run for every proxied request, including the HTTP/2 reuse fast path (:871) and twice on a Basic 407 retry (:889, :910). DispatchViaProxyAsync also rebuilds the tunnel pool key from five strings with two boxed ports per https request (:929, :1374-1377) and the HTTP/2 tunnel key (:868).

**Failure scenario.** A desktop build behind a corporate proxy sending many small requests allocates two collections and several strings per request before any I/O, on top of the direct-path cost.

## Suggested fix
Carry 'absolute-form' and 'strip Proxy-Authorization' as flags on the dispatch (serializer arguments) instead of a rewritten request, and cache the tunnel keys per (proxy, origin).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Absolute-form and strip-Proxy-Authorization are passed as serializer arguments instead of a rewritten request
- [ ] Tunnel pool and HTTP/2 tunnel keys are cached per (proxy, origin)
- [ ] Allocations per proxied request are measured before and after and the header and metadata clones are gone from the reuse path
