title: [Transport] Disposing the transport or pool does not cancel in-flight HTTP/1.1 exchanges or wake requests queued on a per-host permit
body:
## Summary
Dispose disposes the pool and its semaphores while exchanges are still running and requests are waiting for a per-host permit. In-flight requests continue on connections nobody will close, and queued requests wait on semaphores that were disposed under them, which can throw ObjectDisposedException at arbitrary points or hang.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/Tcp/TcpConnectionPool.cs:948`

## Problem
RawSocketTransport.Dispose only disposes the HTTP/2 manager and the pool (RawSocketTransport.cs:2425-2432); there is no transport-lifetime token, and _disposed is checked once at the start of DispatchCoreAsync (:435). TcpConnectionPool.Dispose disposes idle connections and then every SemaphoreSlim (TcpConnectionPool.cs:938-952). Leased connections are not tracked, so an HTTP/1.1 exchange in flight keeps its socket and keeps calling the handler until it completes or its own timeout fires (a streaming body uses CancellationToken.None as the transport read token, RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830). A request waiting in semaphore.WaitAsync(ct) (:462) is never completed: Dispose does not wake async waiters, and the leases that would have released a permit swallow ObjectDisposedException in ReleaseSemaphoreOnce (:250-257). The waiter therefore sits until the request timeout; in the BCL SemaphoreSlim implementations that null the lock object in Dispose, its cancellation path then faults with ArgumentNullException, which MapDispatchAttemptFailure reports as UHttpErrorType.Unknown instead of Timeout/cancellation (RawSocketTransport.cs:827-828). No test queues a waiter and disposes the pool (TcpConnectionPoolTests covers dispose with idle and with returned leases only).

**Failure scenario.** Mobile client with 8 requests in flight to one host and 20 queued; the scene unloads and client.Dispose() runs. The 8 exchanges keep their sockets and deliver callbacks into the torn-down scene; the 20 queued requests stay pending for up to the 45 s request timeout and then fail with an Unknown error. In the Editor without domain reload the leftovers run into the next play session.

## Suggested fix
Give the transport a lifetime CancellationTokenSource linked into every dispatch (cancel it first in Dispose), track outstanding leases so Dispose can dispose their connections, and complete permit waiters with ObjectDisposedException instead of disposing the semaphores under them.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Transport has a lifetime CancellationTokenSource linked into every dispatch and cancelled first in Dispose
- [ ] Outstanding leases are tracked and Dispose disposes their connections
- [ ] Permit waiters complete with ObjectDisposedException instead of the semaphores being disposed under them
- [ ] In-flight requests fail promptly with a transport error when the transport is disposed
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-runtime-07` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: medium. Angle: resource-management.

Verification: Confirmed: a second reviewer re-traced the failure scenario in the code.

Verifier note: Traced. RawSocketTransport.Dispose only disposes the h2 manager and the pool (:2425-2432); _disposed is read once at :435 and in the h2 retry filter (:533); there is no lifetime token linked into timeoutCts (:439-441). TcpConnectionPool.Dispose drains idle connections and disposes every SemaphoreSlim (TcpConnectionPool.cs:938-952); leased connections are not tracked anywhere, so an HTTP/1.1 exchange in flight keeps its socket until it ends or its own timeout fires (streaming bodies read with CancellationToken.None, RawSocketTransport.cs:1826-1830). A request parked in semaphore.WaitAsync(ct) (:462, :489) is not completed by SemaphoreSlim.Dispose, and the permits that would wake it are swallowed as ObjectDisposedException in ReleaseSemaphoreOnce (:250-257), so it waits for its request timeout. The ArgumentNullException-to-Unknown mapping (:827-828) depends on the BCL: implementations before .NET 5 null the lock object in Dispose and the cancellation path then locks on null; Unity's Mono class library is of that generation, but this was not run. No test queues a waiter and disposes the pool (TcpConnectionPoolTests has Dispose_DrainsAllConnections and lease-after-dispose cases only). Scope note: this applies to clients that own their transport; a default-configured client uses the shared HttpTransportFactory.Default and does not dispose it at all (UHttpClient.cs:136-140, :595-600), and UHttpClient.Dispose's doc does not promise cancellation. Bounded by the request timeout, but HTTP/2 requests fail at once on the same Dispose, so the two protocols behave differently.

Related: #168.

title: [Transport] TransportModuleInitializer uses replace semantics and can overwrite a custom transport registration when initializers run lazily
body:
## Summary
The module initializer registers the default raw socket transport with replace semantics. On a runtime that runs module initializers lazily, it can run after the application registered its own transport and silently replace it.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/TransportModuleInitializer.cs:17`

## Problem
TransportModuleInitializer.Initialize (17-21) calls RawSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered, which calls HttpTransportFactory.RegisterUnlessCurrent (RawSocketTransport.cs:89-96). RegisterUnlessCurrent keeps the registration only when the current factories are reference-equal to RawSocketTransport's own delegates; for any other registration it replaces _factory and creates a new Lazy (Runtime/Core/HttpTransportFactory.cs:102-116), which the EnsureRegistered summary states explicitly ('It replaces any other registration (a custom factory or SetForTesting)') and Tests/Runtime/Transport/DefaultTransportRegistrationTests.cs:96-119 assert for the explicit call. A module initializer runs when the runtime first touches a type of the assembly, not at a defined startup point; the class comment only says Unity 2021.3 does not run it reliably, and link.xml:67 preserves the type so it survives stripping. The CA2255 warning for it is baselined (Tools~/ci/analyzer-baseline.txt:15). Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:121 recommends decorating: new CountingTransport(new RawSocketTransport()).

**Failure scenario.** A project without TurboHTTP.Complete (or any CoreCLR host such as the Tools~ harnesses) registers HttpTransportFactory.Register(() => new CountingTransport(new RawSocketTransport())). The first HttpTransportFactory.Default read runs the lambda, 'new RawSocketTransport()' is the first touch of TurboHTTP.Transport, the module initializer fires inside the lambda and replaces the registration: that first client gets the decorator, _lazy now points at a plain RawSocketTransport factory, and every later client silently bypasses the decorator while two default transports exist. Confirm by running DefaultTransportRegistration-style code on Mono with the bootstrap excluded and logging the factory identity before and after the first RawSocketTransport construction.

## Suggested fix
Give the initializer a register-only-if-nothing-is-registered path (a RegisterIfNone variant in HttpTransportFactory), keep the replacing behaviour for the explicit EnsureRegistered call, or delete the module initializer (and its link.xml rule and polyfill attribute) now that the bootstrap is the supported path.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The initializer registers only if nothing is registered (a RegisterIfNone variant in HttpTransportFactory), or the module initializer, its link.xml rule and polyfill attribute are removed
- [ ] The explicit EnsureRegistered call keeps its replacing behaviour
- [ ] A custom transport registered before the initializer runs stays registered
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-design-10` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: architecture.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: The mechanism is as described. TransportModuleInitializer.Initialize calls EnsureRegistered (TransportModuleInitializer.cs:17-21) -> RegisterUnlessCurrent, which replaces _factory and _lazy whenever the current factories are not RawSocketTransport's own delegates (HttpTransportFactory.cs:100-116). The Default getter takes no lock (:156-169), so an initializer that fires inside a custom factory lambda at its first 'new RawSocketTransport()' swaps _lazy while the old Lazy is still producing its value: the first reader gets the custom transport and later readers get a plain RawSocketTransport. No guard distinguishes the implicit call from the explicit one. Whether it happens depends on the runtime: IL2CPP on Unity 2021.3 does not run module initializers, and with TurboHTTP.Complete the bootstrap touches the assembly at SubsystemRegistration (TurboHttpBootstrap.cs:53) before any user registration, so the initializer has already run and is idempotent. It needs a host that runs the initializer lazily and has no bootstrap (Mono without TurboHTTP.Complete, or a CoreCLR harness) plus a factory registration that wraps RawSocketTransport. Note the docs example decorates through UHttpClientOptions.Transport (Documentation~/Modules/Transport.md:118-124), not through HttpTransportFactory.Register, so the documented path is not affected. Closed #1 and #275 dealt with registration but not with this replace-on-lazy-init case.

title: [Transport] allowUnsafeCode is enabled for the whole TurboHTTP.Transport assembly but only two desktop certificate verifier files use it
body:
## Summary
The Transport asmdef allows unsafe code, but only two desktop-only certificate verifier files need it. This disables unsafe-code checks for the entire transport core, which contradicts the rule that unsafe code is confined and makes review harder.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/TurboHTTP.Transport.asmdef:7`

## Problem
rg for 'unsafe' and 'fixed (' over Runtime/Transport (vendored Lib excluded) matches only Runtime/Transport/Tls/MacSecTrustVerifier.cs:26 and Runtime/Transport/Tls/WindowsCertificateVerifier.cs:24 ('internal static unsafe class', fixed pointers for P/Invoke arguments). Both are documented as 'compiled on every platform, installed only on macOS/Windows' and are reached only from ServerCertificateVerifier, the verifier of the opt-in BouncyCastle backend. RawSocketTransport.cs, Connection/, Tcp/ and Internal/ contain no unsafe code, no stackalloc and no P/Invoke; the socket channels use only MemoryMarshal.TryGetArray. The asmdef setting (line 7) therefore permits unsafe code in the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 parsers, HPACK and the pool, where the stated rule ('Only Transport may use unsafe code') gives reviewers no narrower boundary.

**Failure scenario.** A later change adds pointer arithmetic to a parser or HPACK hot path inside the same assembly and passes every gate, because the compiler switch and the module rule already allow it; the two P/Invoke files are also compiled into iOS/Android players that can never call them unless the linker removes them.

## Suggested fix
Move the two verifiers into TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle (their only consumer path) or a small platform asmdef, or rewrite the few fixed blocks with Marshal/GCHandle, and set allowUnsafeCode to false for TurboHTTP.Transport.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The two verifiers move to TurboHTTP.Transport.BouncyCastle or a small platform asmdef, or their fixed blocks are rewritten with Marshal/GCHandle
- [ ] allowUnsafeCode is false for TurboHTTP.Transport
- [ ] The package compiles for Editor, Standalone, iOS and Android; check_repo.py passes
- [ ] a deterministic NUnit regression test under Tests/Runtime/Transport/ fails before the fix and passes after it

title: [Packaging] Transport link.xml keeps preserve=all rules its own comments call unnecessary, rooting RawSocketTransport and widening List<T>, ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore<T> and SslStream
body:
## Summary
link.xml in the Transport module preserves whole types such as RawSocketTransport, List`1, ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1 and three SslStream types, although its comments say the rules are not needed. This roots dead code in the transport and widens preservation for the entire app, defeating stripping.

## Location
- `Runtime/Transport/link.xml:53`

## Problem
link.xml:16-20 preserves System.Net.Security.SslStream, SslClientAuthenticationOptions and SslApplicationProtocol with preserve=all although the comment at 6-8 states the provider calls them statically since #303 and 'the linker already keeps what it uses; these rules stay as defense in depth'. link.xml:52-55 preserves the open generics System.Collections.Generic.List`1 and ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1 with preserve=all although the comment at 45-50 says the static call site in BuildAlpnOptions is what makes IL2CPP generate the instantiation. link.xml:64-69 preserves TransportModuleInitializer and RawSocketTransport with preserve=all although the comment at 59-62 says TurboHttpBootstrap calls RawSocketTransport.EnsureRegistered statically. Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs merges this file into the player link.xml whenever TurboHTTP.Transport.dll is in the build, so the mscorlib and System rules apply to the whole application, not to TurboHTTP. preserve=all on RawSocketTransport keeps every private member, including the unreachable DispatchOnStreamAsync chain (net-design-06) and through it Http11ResponseParser.ParseAsync, CompleteBufferedResponseAsync, ReadChunkedBodyAsync/ReadFixedBodyAsync/ReadToEndAsync and ParsedResponsePool (about 300 lines of buffered-parser code with no production caller).

**Failure scenario.** A game that installs the package and builds IL2CPP with Managed Stripping High gets every member of List<T> kept in mscorlib for all of its own List instantiations, the full SslStream surface (server-side authentication, APM overloads and their dependencies) and all of RawSocketTransport plus the buffered HTTP/1.1 parser, none of which a reflection lookup needs. The size cost is paid by projects that use only a WebSocket or only default HTTPS.

## Suggested fix
Delete the rules whose target is statically referenced (RawSocketTransport, TransportModuleInitializer if it is kept at all, List`1, the three SslStream types) and keep only rules for by-name reflection targets (the System.Configuration ones from #450). If a generic instantiation still needs help, use a [Preserve]d static usage method in the Transport assembly rather than preserve=all on a BCL open generic. Measure with a stripped player build before and after.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Rules whose target is statically referenced are deleted (RawSocketTransport, TransportModuleInitializer if kept, List`1, the three SslStream types)
- [ ] Only rules for by-name reflection targets remain (the System.Configuration ones from #450)
- [ ] Any generic instantiation that still needs help uses a targeted rule or an explicit reference
- [ ] IL2CPP Stripping High build still passes the transport smoke test, and the build size change is recorded

## Context
Source: 2026-11 full-library review, finding `net-design-05` in `Development~/docs/review-2026-11/net.md`, reviewed at commit `0e0f1bc`. Severity: low. Angle: pluggability.

Verification: Plausible: the code is as described; the outcome depends on runtime, device or peer behaviour that a static review cannot settle.

Verifier note: The rules and their comments are as described: SslStream, SslClientAuthenticationOptions and SslApplicationProtocol with preserve=all although the comment says the provider calls them statically and the rules are 'defense in depth' (link.xml:6-8, :15-19); open generics List`1 and ManualResetValueTaskSourceCore`1 with preserve=all in mscorlib (:52-55) although the comment credits the static call site (:46-48); RawSocketTransport and TransportModuleInitializer with preserve=all (:67-68) although the bootstrap calls EnsureRegistered statically (:60-62). TurboHttpLinkerProcessor merges the file whenever the Transport assembly is in the build (Editor/TurboHttpLinkerProcessor.cs:20-23, BuildMergedLinkXml), so the mscorlib/System rules are app-wide. The dead code claim also holds: DispatchOnStreamAsync (RawSocketTransport.cs:1846) has no caller, and SendOnStreamAsync, EmitParsedResponseAsync and Http11ResponseParser.ParseAsync are reached only through it or from tests, so preserve=all is what keeps them.
